entries.title: Go big with these burgers for Father’s Day
entries.summary: <p>There’s no better way to celebrate a meat-eating dad than with a juicy, gloriously messy, double-fisted burger.</p><p>Fire up the grill, toast the buns and lean into indulgence with meaty beef patties layered beneath smoky bacon, oozing cheese and sweet onions softened to a slippery tangle. Swipes of spicy mayo bring a kick of heat and cooling creaminess, while every bite delivers smoky satisfaction worthy of the special occasion.</p><p>With these teetering burgers, there’s little need for sides. Just be sure to pass the napkins (and a cold beverage).</p><h3>Cheesy Bacon Burgers With Roasted Onions and Smoky Mayo</h3><p>Active time: 45 minutes<br>Total time: 45 minutes<br>Yield: Makes 4 burgers</p><p><b>Ingredients</b></p><p><b>Mayo:</b></p><p>1 cup mayonnaise<br>1 garlic clove, grated<br>1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice<br>1 teaspoon smoked sweet paprika<br>1/4 teaspoon chipotle chile powder or cayenne<br>1/2 teaspoon kosher salt</p><p>8 slices thick-cut bacon, divided<br>1 3/4 pounds ground beef (80% lean)<br>Kosher salt<br>1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper<br>2 large sweet yellow onions, halved and thinly sliced<br>4 cheese slices<br>4 buns<br>Butter lettuce leaves<br>8 to 12 dill pickle slices</p><p><b>Directions</b></p><p>Combine the mayo ingredients in a small bowl and stir to blend. Refrigerate until use.</p><p>Finely chop 2 slices of bacon and place in a large bowl. Add the beef, 1 teaspoon salt and the black pepper. Using your hands, gently mix to combine without overmixing.</p><p>Divide the meat into four equal portions and form four patties, each about 3/4 inch thick. Using your thumb or the back of a spoon, make a shallow indentation in the center of each patty. (This will prevent the patties from forming a dome as they cook.) Place the patties on a plate and refrigerate while you prepare the onions and remaining bacon.</p><p>Prepare the grill for direct cooking over medium heat. Preheat a griddle over direct heat, if using.</p><p>Arrange the 6 remaining slices of bacon in a skillet on the stovetop over medium heat (or on the preheated griddle on the grill). Cook until crisp, 6 to 8 minutes. Transfer the bacon to a plate lined with paper towels to drain. When cool enough to handle, break each slice in half.</p><p>Pour off all but 1 tablespoon fat from the skillet or griddle. Add the onions and season with salt. Cook over medium heat until soft and golden brown, 10 to 12 minutes, stirring occasionally. Transfer to a bowl.</p><p>Remove the patties from the refrigerator. Increase the grill heat to medium-high. Grill the patties over direct heat until cooked to your desired doneness, 8 to 10 minutes for medium, turning once or twice.</p><p>When the patties are nearly cooked to your desired doneness, place a cheese slice on each patty to melt. While the cheese melts, toast the buns, cut sides down, on the grill grates.</p><p>To build each burger, spread the bottom half of each bun with the mayo, place a lettuce leaf on the bun and top with a patty. Layer the onions, 2 to 3 bacon pieces, and 2 to 3 pickles over the patty. Spread the top half of the bun with more mayo. Close the bun and serve at once.</p>

entries.title: Ald. Ray Lopez plans to try again to hold parents accountable for actions of their kids
entries.summary: <p>Three months ago, Southwest Side Ald. Ray Lopez (15th) tried to hold Chicago parents accountable for curfew violations, street racing, and drug, alcohol and firearms offenses committed by their children.</p><p>His attempt to use parental responsibility to, as he put it, “create better parents” was <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/03/03/parental-responsibility-ordinance-vote-curfew-graffiti-crime-teens" >shot down </a>by a City Council committee — even after Lopez offered to entertain amendments that would have softened the potential legal blow to parents and legal guardians.</p><p>The debate showcased the Council’s political divide. Conservative alderpersons, who are among the police union’s staunchest supporters, want to get tougher on crime. Democratic socialists and other progressives seem more, or at least equally, concerned about preserving individual rights.</p><p>At Wednesday’s City Council meeting, Lopez plans to try again to force parents to pay more attention to where their kids are going in an effort stop large groups of young people summoned by social media from turning violent.</p><p>Lopez plans to use a parliamentary maneuver to not only resurrect the ordinance that received a “Do Not Pass” recommendation in the Committee on Public Safety, but to substitute a new version of it with even stronger consequences for parents whose kids cross the line.</p><p>One of the City Council’s most conservative members and staunchest police supporters, Lopez believes the political dynamic has changed since the March vote rejecting his parental responsibility ordinance.</p><p>“Since March, we’ve had more than a dozen teen takeovers. Hyde Park was destroyed in Ald. [Desmon] Yancy’s ward by 500 youths stomping through Hyde Park Boulevard. We’ve had numerous events downtown and in the neighborhoods. And we continue to have street takeovers involving vehicles doing doughnuts and setting the pavement on fire,” Lopez said.</p><p>“There’s more of an appetite now — especially as aldermen gear up to go knocking on doors asking for people's votes to stay in office. They know that people want to see City Council take some action.”</p><p>Mayor Brandon Johnson has long opposed stricter curfew laws and punitive measures like holding parents accountable. He has argued that investing in young people and their long-neglected neighborhoods — not punishing them and their parents — is the answer to keeping teen gatherings from turning violent.</p><p>At a City Hall news conference Tuesday, Johnson made it clear that his position on such politically volatile issues has not changed.</p><p>“I’ve said from the very beginning it’s not just about accountability. It’s about opportunity as well. That’s why I’ve called on the business community, the philanthropic community, our faith-based organizations, [and] community-based organizations to invest in safe spaces — and people are doing that,” Johnson said.</p><p>The mayor commended the Art Institute for “creating a space for over 500 teenagers to hang out” at the world-renowned art museum. He called that program an example of what works.</p><p>“As far as increasing penalties, we know what criminalization does, particularly for more vulnerable communities. It has not led to creating safer spaces,” Johnson said. “We have to do what works. So I’m going to continue to call for the level of opportunity and investment. And when individuals act outside the confines... of the law, those individuals should be held accountable.”</p><p>Chicago already holds parents responsible for spray painting and graffiti by their kids. Lopez says that effort helps explain a “precipitous decline” in such vandalism.</p><p>He says he believes the situation would be the same if parents were held accountable for “willfully or knowingly” allowing a minor under their care to violate a broader array of crimes that include curfew violations; illegal drag racing; drifting or jumping on vehicles; illicit drug or alcohol use, and access to firearms or paintball guns.</p><p>His new version includes even stronger penalties for parents accused of “contributing to the delinquency of a minor” who commits any one of those crimes. The parental fine would start at $1,000, which adults could avoid by opting for community service and family counseling at the parent’s expense.</p><p>But the fines could rise to $10,000 for the parents of repeat offenders and young people who use vehicles to create street takeover events. And the fines would double, then triple for the second and third offenses within a one-year period.</p><p>Lopez said he will try to suspend the rules for immediate consideration of the stronger ordinance. Lopez argued that the mere attempt will put his colleagues on the spot.</p><p>“It’ll be really a testament before the entire body just how committed we are to ensuring that we are breaking this cycle of youthful craziness in the city of Chicago by holding parents accountable for their children,” he said. "We have already seen this month just how wild and dangerous the streets have become, because we refuse to hold parents accountable and the youth accountable. I, for one... don't want that on our hands." </p>
entries.author: Fran Spielman

entries.title: This Sky season is an exercise in waiting
entries.summary: <p>Close, but not quite. That about sums up the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky" target="_blank" >Sky</a> right now.</p><p>They’ve played well against playoff-caliber teams in their last two games but lost both in the final minutes. Their injured players, Courtney Vandersloot and DiJonai Carrington, are making progress but still don’t have specific timelines to return.</p><p>Vandersloot is the closest, now practicing at full speed again. But she still won’t be available this week against the Liberty and Wings.</p><p>“I got a little bit of muscle to build still,” Vandersloot told the Sun-Times.</p><p>She’s working to close the gap between her left and right knee. After a year of rehab, she’s being careful not to rush the final step.</p><p>It’s the smart move. But for a team that has lost seven of its last eight and is fighting not to let the season slip away, the waiting is painful.</p><p>Cruel, even.</p><p>Vandersloot is right there. She’s impressing everyone in practice and is convinced she can bring comfort and structure to the offense as soon as she returns.</p><p>“That’s where my strength is,” Vandersloot said. “Getting the offense to flow and run well. I can get people the shots that they’re used to getting. But I think the biggest thing is the leadership out there. People feel comfortable when I’m on the floor with them. I’m hoping that helps us a little bit in certain moments.”</p><p>From the sideline, Vandersloot sees some momentum building in team’s most recent performances <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky/2026/06/15/skylar-diggins-knows-small-mistakes-will-cost-sky-against-liberty" >against the Dream and Fever.</a></p><p>“We’re responding well,” Vandersloot said. “We’re sticking together, making our own runs. We have certain lapses at times where we can’t make a shot or whatever it may be, and we don’t just quit. We keep fighting. I think that’s been the biggest difference in the last couple games.</p><p>“The offense is flowing a little bit better. In my opinion, when that’s clicking, all of a sudden it becomes a little bit easier to defend. Coaches will say the opposite, but that’s how I see the game.”</p><p>The Sky’s offense ranks 13th out of 15 teams this season. But over the last two games, that's jumped to 8th.</p><p>It’s amazing what hitting shots will do.</p><p>Coach Tyler Marsh believes the Sky generate open looks as well as any team in the league. But the season has basically been an exercise in waiting for the shots to fall.</p><p>They’ve made fewer than 30% of their three-pointers in nine of 13 games.</p><p>They’ve shot 75% or worse from the free-throw line in more than half their games, a real shame for a team that takes the second-most attempts in the league.</p><p>“I think when you lose a couple games, that rim gets a little tighter,” Vandersloot said. “Even the best shooting teams go through times where you’re not making shots. That’s part of the game. For us, it’s just finding other ways to score when those nights are happening.”</p><p>Which makes it encouraging that, despite the last two losses, the shots have started to fall.</p><p>Point guard Skylar Diggins has hit six of her 10 attempts from deep in that span, including the three-pointer that sent the Fever game to overtime. The lid came off for rookie guard Sydney Taylor, too. Taylor, who leads the team in three-point attempts, went 4-for-7 against the Fever.</p><p>“Once we get that going, that kind of stuff is contagious,” Vandersloot said. “If you can get somebody that can start hitting some shots, that rim looks a little bit bigger.”</p><p>Maybe the Sky are on the cusp of a breakthrough. Or maybe they’ll just have to keep waiting.</p>

entries.title: What to know about the Obama Center's opening weekend and beyond
entries.summary: <p>With the Obama Presidential Center set to open this week, the Chicago Sun-Times is answering some of the most frequently asked questions about the festivities planned for opening weekend and beyond.</p><h3>How can I watch or attend the opening ceremony Thursday? </h3><p>The Obama Center’s Thursday grand opening is invitation-only but will be livestreamed on <a class="Link" href="https://click.email.obama.org/?qs=ABB7InYiOjEsImQiOjQ5MDl9AAoAAAAAAbsuAtBvtP0FF0ZoeqCa-_UkuLMhUDrsFJm4wvEnx4UqGDYN2ZaeSkKHY5_Q-op7cfTu354iVeiztTmphJMPhcceeEbzmT_SG8M" target="_blank" ><u>Obama.org</u></a>, as well as on the Obama Foundation’s social media accounts.</p><h3>Who is performing?</h3><p>The 11 a.m. ceremony is <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/arts-and-culture/2026/06/16/obama-presidential-center-opening-ceremony-lineup-to-include-stevie-wonder-bruce-springsteen" target="_blank" >slated to feature several big names</a>. Some of them include Stevie Wonder, Bruce Springsteen, Common, Eddie Vedder, the Roots, Christina Aguilera, Jennifer Hudson, John Legend, Marc Anthony, Tems, U2’s Bono and The Edge and actress and producer Marsai Martin.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/05/06/obama-presidential-center-tickets-sales-demand-sold-out-june-july" >Obama Presidential Center sells out first month hours after tickets become available</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/arts-and-culture/2026/06/16/obama-presidential-center-opening-ceremony-lineup-to-include-stevie-wonder-bruce-springsteen" >Obama Presidential Center opening ceremony lineup to include Stevie Wonder, Bruce Springsteen</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p><h3>How can I attend the Obama Center after the opening ceremony?</h3><p>The center opens to the public on Friday, Juneteenth. Public events continue through that Sunday, Father’s Day.</p><p>Opening weekend tickets <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/05/06/obama-presidential-center-tickets-sales-demand-sold-out-june-july" target="_blank" >sold out in hours</a>, and reservations for Illinois Free Days — Tuesdays — are sold out past October.</p><p>Activities on opening weekend include:<br></p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-9bd15900-69c8-11f1-90be-5f2924764417"><li>Performances and programs featuring Obama Presidential Center commissioned artists</li><li>Storytime and hands-on activities at the center’s Chicago Public Library branch</li><li>Double Dutch performances and crochet jump rope-making in the Home Court building</li><li>Interactive experiences in the Eleanor Roosevelt Fruit and Vegetable Garden centered on growing food</li><li>Talks in the center’s auditorium</li><li>Guided and self-guided audio tours</li><li>"Sports and play stations” at its Home Court athletic center with mascots from Chicago's teams</li></ul><h3>What streets will be closed for opening weekend?</h3><p>The city's Office of Emergency Management and Communication is maintaining a <a class="Link" href="https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/oem/provdrs/emerg_mang/news/2026/June/UpdatedObamaPresidentialOpening.html" target="_blank" >list of street closures</a>. </p><p>The schedule includes these closures:</p><p>From 6 a.m. Monday to 6 a.m. Friday:<br></p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-9bd15901-69c8-11f1-90be-5f2924764417"><li>Midway Plaisance, from Dorchester to Stony Island Avenue both ways</li><li>Blackstone Avenue, from 59th Street to Midway Plaisance</li><li>Cornell Avenue, from Stony Island Avenue to 57th Street</li><li>Stony Island Avenue, from Midway Plaisance to 63rd Street</li><li>Stony Island Avenue northbound, from 59th Street to 57th Street</li><li>59th Street southbound, from South Harper Avenue to Stony Island Avenue</li></ul><p>From 6 a.m. Monday to 11:59 p.m. Saturday:<br></p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-9bd18010-69c8-11f1-90be-5f2924764417"><li>Midway Plaisance, from Woodlawn to Blackstone avenues</li><li>Dorchester Street, from 59th to 60th Street</li></ul><p>From 6 a.m. Wednesday to 6 a.m. Friday:<br></p><ul class="rte2-style-ul" id="rte-9bd18011-69c8-11f1-90be-5f2924764417"><li>Woodlawn Avenue, from 59th to 60th Street</li><li>Midway Plaisance, from Ellis to Woodlawn Avenue</li></ul><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/art/2026/06/16/portrait-akunyili-crosby-obamas-life-story-debuts-obama-presidential-center" >New portrait showing the Obamas and their life story debuts at Obama Presidential Center</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/art/2026/06/16/norman-teague-bench-obama-presidential-center" >The unlikely standout at the Obama Presidential Center? This bench designed by Norman Teague</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p><h3>How can I attend after opening weekend?</h3><p>Tickets are sold out for June and half of July, though the calendar has openings into November. </p><p>Tickets cost $30. There’s a $4 discount for Illinois residents, a $3 discount for out-of-state kids and $11 off for in-state kids. Tickets cannot be returned, transferred or sold.</p><p>CTA expanded service on the No. 10 route, which was renamed the No. 10 Obama Presidential Center/Museum of Science & Industry Express. Due to street closures opening weekend, the closest No. 10 stop will be the Griffin Museum of Science and Industry.</p><p>Metra's Electric Line runs closest to the center. The Red and Green Lines also connect to the No. 6, No. 15 and No. 28 buses, which also run near the center.</p><h3>What other events are being held through the summer?</h3><p>In July and August, the center will host a series of talks, films and events for the nation’s 250th anniversary titled “You Are America.” It kicks off with a free Independence Day celebration called “The People’s Fourth,” featuring live music, self-guided tours and family-friendly activities.</p><p>Summer Garden Gatherings will be hosted in the fruit and vegetable garden every other week from July 12 to Sept. 20. A walk-run club for those 50-years or older called "At Your Pace" will meet at the center on Thursday mornings from Aug. 6 to Oct. 8.</p><p>On Aug. 4, an all-ages celebration of President Barack Obama’s birthday will be held.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/real-estate/2026/06/05/barack-obama-airbnb-presidential-center-chicago-affordable-housing-displacement-gentrification" >As short-term rentals increase near the Obama Center, housing advocates say affordable units are disappearing</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/in-the-loop-with-sasha-ann-simons/2026/06/16/how-well-has-chicago-protected-residents-near-the-obama-center-from-getting-pushed-out" >How well has Chicago protected residents near the Obama Center from getting pushed out?</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://www.wbez.org/in-the-loop-with-sasha-ann-simons/2026/06/16/potential-tourism-boom-around-obama-center-could-affect-affordability-for-residents" >Potential tourism boom around Obama Center could affect affordability for residents</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Englewood development wants to make 59th Street a 'corridor to watch'
entries.summary: <p>Hundreds of Englewood residents celebrated the groundbreaking of a long-awaited project that could help make 59th Street “the corridor to watch,” Resident Association of Greater Englewood Executive Director Asiaha Butler said.</p><p>The RAGE's $6.4 million mixed-use development — dubbed The Re-Up — will turn a vacant building at 1210 W. 59th St. into its new headquarters, with retail space for Black-owned businesses. The organization is now at 6620 S. Union Ave.</p><p>Butler dreamed up the project in 2021 as an “economic justice strategy," after the 2020 civil unrest and Black Lives Matter protests in her South Side community. </p><p>She said during Monday's groundbreaking, "there were tears." </p><p>“People who possibly felt that they didn’t have a voice, their voices got heard. What they wanted, we organized around and co-created together,” she said.</p><p>The organization received a $2.5 million grant through the city's Neighborhood Opportunity Fund, marking its first city grant. It also received property tax incentives that will generate over $200,000 in savings over 12 years, according to a news release from Mayor Brandon Johnson’s office.</p><p>“The Re-Up reflects the vision, determination and organizing power of Englewood residents who have invested in their neighborhood and refused to let disinvestment define its future,” Johnson said in the release.</p><p>RAGE purchased the former Leon’s Bar-B-Que spot in 2023 for $35,000, after it sat vacant for over a decade. </p><p>Their redevelopment project stalled as they waited for permits to be approved, Butler said. Construction started last year, and the project is expected to be finished in the first quarter of 2027.</p><p>Butler said she’s happy to be “extremely patient,” as she learns the process.</p><div Pasciak LaRiviere/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Englewood has long been a South Side neighborhood that mobilizes its community members to bring more resources to residents, including a push to support Black-owned businesses.</p><p>Butler said some local businesses interested in leasing space during the early stages of the project ended up closing.</p><p>“Shortly after COVID, [businesses] were really hurting, and some of the restaurants who had a letter of interest for The Re-Up went out of business,” she said.</p><p>The Re-Up, which stands for the RAGE Economic Upliftment Project, is meant to serve as a catalyst for the area's revitalization. The 7,950-square-foot building will have two tenants on the first floor, and the second floor will be RAGE's headquarters.</p><p>RAGE and residents are still considering the type of tenants they’d like to see, Butler said. Some ideas have included restaurants, retail, offices, a gym or wellness center, as well as a space for businesses to print.</p><p>“We lack so many amenities and so many types of businesses, and so we've heard a variety of different things,” she said.</p><p>Any tenant at the property will be required to hire from the community — employees who live in the 60621 or 60636 ZIP codes. It’s estimated that the project will create 50 permanent jobs, with a goal of creating 150 new jobs over three years.</p><p>Butler said the development will help unify Englewood and West Englewood. It will also complement other investments nearby, such as the Englewood Nature Trail and plans to expand Dion’s Dream Chicago and the Growing Home Englewood Farm Stand.</p><p>“[Fifty-ninth Street] is going to be the corridor to watch, especially coming from Midway to the Obama Center. You can take one bus and go all the way there,” Butler said.</p><p>The Obama Presidential Center, about 4 miles east of The Re-Up, will <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/05/27/obama-presidential-center-opening-weekend" >open to the public</a> Friday.</p><p>“It’s nothing but love and pride,” Butler said of Monday's celebration, which drew about 400 people. “[Residents] are excited to see something happening here.”</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/05/27/obama-presidential-center-opening-weekend" >Obama Center releases grand opening weekend events schedule</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>
